correctness.rationale: The property quantifies over every pair x,y in any real normed space dim>=3, and the median is minimized over the whole ambient X, not just its planar triangle. Given a noncollinear triangle enclosing origin, positive rescaling v1+v2+v3=0 yields 3sum_i||v_i||<=2sum_i||v_j-v_k||. If any d_i>(3/2)||v_i||, scaling the opposite vector by t=( (2/3)d_i/||v_i|| -1)/2>0 reaches ratio 2/3. If all d_i=(3/2)||v_i||, equality forces all three norms equal h; a norm-one Hahn–Banach functional norming v1 gives ||2v1-v2||>=5h/2 whereas ||2v1+v2||=3h/2. Therefore the continuous ratio ||2v1+v2-2t v3||/||2v1-v2|| starts <=3/5 and crosses 2/3 at some t>0, overcoming Fang–Liu zero-scaling obstruction. If origin lies on the triangle edge, rescale opposing edge vectors and the third explicitly. Radial-invariance of Fermat medianhood at origin is proved by a convexity inequality and invertible positive scaling. Starting from a planar median inside any equilateral triangle, the endpoint property gives an ambient median in the transformed triangle, forcing the planar center also to be an ambient median and allowing Pakhrou Corollary 5.6 to imply a Hilbert norm. In a Hilbert space metric projection into the triangle decreases distance to vertices and supplies the converse even without completeness. Independent exact rational hexagon example verifies saturated equality case (b1=2v1, b2=v2, b3=v3/12 has norm ratio 2/3); no finite check is used for arbitrary spaces.

value.rationale: Closing a sharply delimited endpoint omitted in a recent Hilbert-space characterization is a motivated mathematical boundary problem, not a routine parameter substitution: strict positivity fails for the existing scaling argument exactly at 2/3. The norming-functional 3/5 buffer is a genuine structural lemma for all real normed planes and makes the characterization valid in non-smooth noncomplete spaces. This is a reusable test of Hilbertianity at an otherwise excluded boundary.

final_claim: For real normed spaces of dimension at least three, the Fermat–Torricelli ambient convex-hull median property tested only on triples (0,x,y) with ||x+y||=(2/3)||x-y|| characterizes inner-product norms. New endpoint rescaling lemma also covers equality of the 3/2 separation bound with strictly positive third factor.
